title: Area3D space override Combine-Replace not functioning as Described
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in v4.6.beta1.official [d743736f8], v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1], v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]



### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Linux Mint 22.1 (Xia) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (nvidia; 575.57.08) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.24 GiB memory

### Issue description

Space Override "Combine-Replace" for Area3D states that "This area adds its gravity/damping values to whatever has been calculated so far (in priority) order), ignoring any lower priority areas." Implying they should combine when the priorities are the same. However when testing it acts nearly identical to the "Replace" mode when Area3D's are set to the same priority.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Zero out the Default Gravity Vector in Project Settings
2. Create a 3D scene with 2 overlapping Area3D's with any given collision shape
3. Set the gravity space override of both of them to Combine-Replace (make sure both are the same priority)
4. Set one Area3D to have a gravity direction with y set to -1 and the other to 1 (this should in theory cancel out the 2 areas gravity)
5. Add a rigid body of any kind (as long as its visible) and add a camera to view the scene
6. Rigid body doesn't stay put, but will instead be affected by only 1 Area3D

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[area-3d-bug-report.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24147897/area-3d-bug-report.zip)
